1.contenido: 1. Talking about reconciliation and penance is, for the men and women of our time, an invitation to rediscover – translated into one's own language – the same words with which Our Savior and Master Jesus Christ wanted to inaugurate his preaching: “Convert and believe in the Gospel”[1] that is, welcome the Good News of love, of adoption as children of God and, consequently, of fraternity.

2.contenido: 2. These divisions are manifested in the relationships between people and groups, but also at the level of broader collectivities: Nations against Nations and blocks of Countries facing each other in an eager search for hegemony. At the root of ruptures it is not difficult to identify conflicts that, instead of being resolved through dialogue, become more acute in confrontation and contrast.

3.contenido: 3. However, the same inquisitive gaze, if it is sufficiently sharp, captures in the most vivid part of the division an unmistakable desire, on the part of men of good will and true Christians, to mend the fractures, to heal the wounds, to establish an essential unity at all levels. Such a desire entails in many a true nostalgia for reconciliation, even when they do not use this word.

4.contenido: 4. Therefore, every institution or organization dedicated to serving man and interested in saving him in his fundamental dimensions, must direct a penetrating look at reconciliation, in order to deepen its meaning and full scope, drawing the necessary consequences for action.

5.contenido: 5. At the beginning of this Apostolic Exhortation, the extraordinary page of St. Luke is presented to my spirit, which I have already tried to illustrate in a previous Document of mine[19]. I am referring to the parable of the prodigal son[20].

6.contenido: 6. But the parable also depicts the older brother who refuses his place at the banquet. He reproaches the younger brother for his strayings and the father for the welcome given to the prodigal son while he, sober and hard-working, faithful to his father and the house, has never been allowed, he says, to celebrate a party with friends. A sign that he has not understood the father's goodness. Until this brother, too sure of himself and his own merits, jealous and lackadaisical, full of bitterness and rage, is converted and reconciled with his father and brother, the banquet will not yet be fully the celebration of encounter and discovery.

7.contenido: 7. As can be deduced from the parable of the prodigal son, reconciliation is a gift from God, an initiative of his. But our faith teaches us that this initiative takes shape in the mystery of Christ the redeemer, the reconciler, who frees man from sin in all its forms. St. Paul himself does not hesitate to summarize in this task and function the incomparable mission of Jesus of Nazareth, Word and Son of God made man.

8.contenido: 8. But as Saint Leo the Great said, speaking of the passion of Christ, "everything that the Son of God worked and taught for the reconciliation of the world, we do not know only through the history of his past actions, but we also feel it in the effectiveness of what he does in the present"[32].

9.contenido: 9. My venerated Predecessor Paul VI has had the merit of making clear that, to be evangelizing, the Church must begin by showing itself to be evangelized, that is, open to the full and complete announcement of the Good News of Jesus Christ, listening to it and putting it into practice[37]. I too, when collecting in an organic document the reflections of the IV General Assembly of the Synod, have spoken of a Church that catechizes itself to the extent that it carries out catechesis[38].

10.contenido: 10. Because it is a reconciled and reconciling community, the Church cannot forget that at the very origin of its gift and its reconciling mission is the initiative full of compassionate and merciful love of the God who is love[41] and who created men out of love[42]; He has created them to live in friendship with Him and in mutual communion.

11.contenido: 11. The Church has the mission of announcing this reconciliation and being its sacrament in the world. Sacrament, that is, sign and instrument of reconciliation, the Church is by different titles of different value, but all of them aimed at obtaining what the divine initiative of mercy wants to grant to men.

12.contenido: 12. The reconciling mission is proper to the entire Church, and in a particular way to that which has already been admitted to the full participation of divine glory with the Virgin Mary, with the Angels and the Saints, who contemplate and adore the thrice-holy God. Church of heaven, Church of earth, and Church of purgatory are mysteriously united in this cooperation with Christ in reconciling the world to God.

13.contenido: 13. As the apostle Saint John writes: «If we say that we are without sin, we deceive ourselves and the truth is not with us. If we recognize our sins, He who is faithful and just will forgive us our sins”[56]. These inspired words, written at the dawn of the Church, introduce us better than any other human expression to the topic of sin, which is closely related to that of reconciliation. Such words focus on the problem of sin in its anthropological perspective as an integral part of the truth about man, but they immediately frame it in the divine horizon, in which sin is confronted with the truth of divine love, just, generous and faithful, which is manifested above all with forgiveness and redemption. For this reason, Saint John himself writes a little later that "if our heart reproaches us for something, God is greater than our heart"[57].

14.contenido: 14. If we read the biblical page about the city and the tower of Babel in the new light of the Gospel, and compare it with that other page about the fall of our first parents, we can draw valuable elements for an awareness of the mystery of sin. This expression, in which the echo of what Saint Paul writes about the mystery of iniquity[66] resonates, is aimed at making us perceive what is dark and incomprehensible hidden in sin. This is undoubtedly the work of man's freedom; but within its own human weight there are factors at work due to which sin is located beyond the human, in that limit zone where the conscience, will and sensitivity of man are in contact with the dark forces that, according to Saint Paul, work in the world until they take over it[67].

15.contenido: 15. In the biblical narratives mentioned above, the break with God dramatically leads to the division between the brothers.

16.contenido: 16. Sin, in the true and proper sense, is always an act of the person, because it is a free act of the individual person, and not precisely of a group or a community. This man may be conditioned, pressured, pushed by not a few or slight external factors; just as it may also be subject to tendencies, flaws and customs linked to its personal condition. In many cases, these external and internal factors can attenuate, to a greater or lesser extent, their freedom and, therefore, their responsibility and guilt. But it is a truth of faith, also confirmed by our experience and reason, that the human person is free. This truth cannot be ignored in order to download the sin of individuals into external realities – structures, systems, others. After all, this would mean eliminating the dignity and freedom of the person, which are revealed - even if in such a negative and disastrous way - also in this responsibility for the sin committed. And thus, in each man there is nothing so personal and non-transferable as the merit of virtue or the responsibility of guilt.

17.contenido: 17. But here is, in the mystery of sin, a new dimension on which the mind of man has never stopped meditating: that of its gravity. It is an inevitable question, to which the Christian conscience has never given up giving an answer: why and to what extent is sin serious in the offense it makes to God and in its impact on man? The Church has its doctrine on the matter, and reaffirms it in its essential elements, even knowing that it is not always easy, in concrete situations, to clearly demarcate the boundaries.

18.contenido: 18. Through the Gospel read in the ecclesial communion, the Christian conscience has acquired, throughout the generations, a fine sensitivity and a keen perception of the ferments of death, which are contained in sin. Sensitivity and capacity for perception also to individuate these ferments in the multiple forms assumed by sin, in the many aspects under which it presents itself. This is what is called the sense of sin.

19.contenido: 19. To know sin it was necessary to look at its nature, which has been made known to us by the revelation of the economy of salvation: sin is the mysterium iniquitatis. But in this economy sin is not the protagonist, much less the winner. It contrasts as an antagonist with another operating principle, which “using a beautiful and suggestive expression of Saint Paul” we can call mysterium or sacramentum pietatis. Man's sin would prove victorious and, in the end, destructive; God's saving plan would remain incomplete or even defeated if this mysterium pietatis had not been inserted into the dynamics of history to overcome man's sin.

20.contenido: 20. It is very significant that, to present this "mysterium pietatis", Paul, without establishing a grammatical relationship with the preceding text[105], simply transcribes three lines from a Christological Hymn, which "according to the opinion of accredited scholars" was used in the Hellenic-Christian communities.

21.contenido: 21. But there is another aspect in the mysterium pietatis; God's piety toward the Christian must correspond to the Christian's piety toward God. In this second meaning, piety ([+[0]+]) means precisely the behavior of the Christian, who responds to God's paternal piety with his filial piety.

22.contenido: 22. Thus the Word of Scripture, by revealing to us the mystery of piety, opens human intelligence to conversion and reconciliation, understood not as mere abstractions, but as concrete Christian values ​​to conquer in our daily lives.

23.contenido: 23. Arousing conversion and penitence in the heart of man and offering him the gift of reconciliation is the innate mission of the Church, continuator of the redemptive work of its divine Founder. This is a mission that does not end in mere theoretical statements or in the proposal of an ethical ideal that is not accompanied by operational energies, but rather tends to be expressed in precise ministerial functions in order to a concrete practice of penance and reconciliation.

24.contenido: 24. To promote penitence and reconciliation, the Church has at its disposal mainly two means, which have been entrusted to it by its Founder himself: catechesis and the Sacraments. Its use, always considered by the Church as fully in accordance with the demands of its salvific mission and corresponding, at the same time, to the demands and spiritual needs of men of all times, can be carried out in old and new forms and modes, among which it will be good to remember particularly what, following my predecessor Paul VI, we can call the method of dialogue.

25.contenido: 25. Dialogue is for the Church, in a certain sense, a means and, above all, a way of developing its action in the contemporary world.

26.contenido: 26. In the vast area in which the Church has the mission to act through dialogue, the pastoral care of penance and reconciliation is addressed to the members of the body of the Church, above all, with an adequate catechesis on the two different and complementary realities to which the Synodal Fathers have given particular importance, and which they have highlighted in some of the concluding Propositions: precisely penance and reconciliation. Catechesis, then, is the first means that must be used.

27.contenido: 27. The second means of divine institution that the Church offers to the pastoral care of penance and reconciliation are the Sacraments.

28.contenido: 28. The Synod, in all its phases and at all levels of its development, has considered with the greatest attention that sacramental sign that represents and at the same time carries out penance and reconciliation. This Sacrament certainly does not exhaust in itself the concepts of conversion and reconciliation. Indeed, since its origins the Church has known and valued numerous and varied forms of penance: some liturgical or paraliturgical, ranging from the penitential act of the Mass to propitiatory functions and pilgrimages; others of an ascetic nature, such as fasting. However, of all the acts, none is more significant, nor more divinely effective, nor more elevated and at the same time accessible in its own rite, than the sacrament of Penance.

29.contenido: 29. The first fundamental data is offered to us in the Holy Books of the Old and New Testaments about the mercy of the Lord and his forgiveness. In the Psalms and in the preaching of the prophets, the term merciful is perhaps the one most often attributed to the Lord, contrary to the persistent cliché, according to which the God of the Old Testament is presented above all as severe and punitive. Thus, in a Psalm, a long wisdom discourse, following the tradition of the Exodus, the benign action of God in the midst of his people is evoked again. Such an action, even in its anthropomorphic representation, is perhaps one of the most eloquent Old Testament proclamations of divine mercy. Suffice it to quote the verse here: «But he is merciful and forgave iniquity, and did not exterminate them, often restraining his anger so that his anger would not be vented. He remembered that they were flesh, a breath that passes and does not return"[157].

30.contenido: 30. From the revelation of the value of this ministry and the power to forgive sins, conferred by Christ on the Apostles and their successors, awareness of the sign of forgiveness, granted through the Sacrament of Penance, has developed in the Church. This gives the certainty that the Lord Jesus himself instituted and entrusted to the Church - as a gift of his kindness and his "philanthropy"[172] offered to all - a special Sacrament for the forgiveness of sins committed after Baptism.

31.contenido: 31. The aforementioned truths, reaffirmed with force and clarity by the Synod, and present in the Propositiones, can be summarized in the following convictions of faith, around which the other affirmations of Catholic doctrine on the Sacrament of Penance are gathered.

32.contenido: 32. Following the indications of the Second Vatican Council, the Ordo Paenitentiae has authorized three forms that, always preserving the essential elements, allow the celebration of the Sacrament of Penance to be adapted to certain pastoral circumstances.

33.contenido: 33. In the new liturgical order and, more recently, in the new Code of Canon Law[196], the conditions that legitimize recourse to the "rite of reconciliation of several penitents with confession and general absolution" are specified. The rules and provisions given on this point, the result of mature and balanced consideration, must be accepted and applied, avoiding any type of arbitrary interpretation.

34.contenido: 34. I think that I must make at this moment an allusion, although very brief, to a pastoral case that the Synod wanted to deal with âas far as it was possible to do so, and which also contemplates one of the Propositions. I am referring to certain situations, not uncommon today, in which some Christians find themselves, desirous of continuing sacramental religious practice, but who are prevented by their personal situation, which is in opposition to the obligations freely assumed before God and the Church. These are situations that appear particularly delicate and almost insoluble.

35.contenido: 35. At the end of this Document, I echo and wish to repeat to all of you the exhortation that the first Bishop of Rome, in a critical hour at the beginning of the Church, addressed "to the chosen foreigners in the diaspora... chosen according to the foreknowledge of God the Father." "Everyone has the same mind, be compassionate, fraternal, merciful, humble"[200]. The Apostle recommended: "Let everyone have the same mind..."; but he immediately continued pointing out the sins against concord and peace, which must be avoided: "Not returning evil for evil or insult for insult; On the contrary, blessing, for to this we have been called, to be heirs of the blessing. And he concluded with a word of encouragement and hope: "And who will harm you if you are zealous promoters of good?"[201]
